title: Onprem node provisioning and Terraform debug checklist
content:
Purpose:
This is a working checklist + troubleshooting playbook for common on-prem / VPC deployment failures we see during initial installs, node provisioning, and during rolling upgrades. Focus is on quick triage, small terraform workarounds, and minimal smoke-tests to confirm a recovered state.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: SREs and solutions engineers doing private deployments or supporting customers during upgrades.
- Scope: provisioning (Terraform + cloud-init), container runtime and drivers, service startup, model artifact loading, and common network/DNS/MTU traps. Not a complete runbook for security incidents.

Quick triage flow (1–3 minute healthcheck):
1) Ask customer: what changed? (upgrade plan, kernel/driver, firewall rule, new subnet).
2) Confirm overall cluster state: `kubectl get nodes -o wide` or `rctlctl node list` (if self-managed small cluster). Expected: all nodes Ready, not NotReady or Unknown.
   - If NotReady: `kubectl describe node <node>` -> check kubelet, disk pressure, cgroup driver mismatch.
3) Check control-plane: `systemctl status redwood-agent` or `journalctl -u kubelet -n 200` for obvious errors.
4) Check docker/containerd: `docker ps` or `crictl ps` and `journalctl -u containerd -n 200`.
5) Quick network test: from a node `curl -sS http://169.254.169.254 || echo no-metadata` and `host api.internal.redwood.local`. DNS/DHCP/MTU issues often show here.

Common failure categories and quick fixes:
A) Terraform state/locking issues
- Symptom: `terraform apply` hangs at plan/apply with lock errors or fails with provider mismatches.
- Quick checks: `terraform state list` (ensure you are using the same workspace), `terraform -version` and `terraform providers lock` to confirm provider versions.
- Workarounds:
  - If remote state lock left by crash: `terraform force-unlock <LOCK_ID>` after confirming no other in-flight applies.
  - If module drift: import existing resource into tfstate: `terraform import module.network.aws_vpc.vpc vpc-12345` then re-run plan.
  - If provider plugin mismatch across machines: pin provider versions in `required_providers` block and run `terraform init -upgrade` on the CI machine.

B) Node provisioning failures (cloud-init, SSH, GPU drivers)
- Symptoms: node stays in provisioning or fails to register; nvidia-smi missing; kernel module errors.
- Checks: `/var/log/cloud-init.log`, `dmesg | tail -n 50`, `lsmod | grep nvidia`, `nvidia-smi`
- Fixes:
  - cloud-init kept failing: re-run `cloud-init single --name cc_ssh` or check user-data size limits. Clear cloud-init state: `cloud-init clean` then re-run boot config.
  - Drivers: Ensure kernel headers installed before driver compile. If CUDA mismatch: check model-serving container base image vs host driver compatibility matrix. Short-term workaround: use host driver compatible container or use software fallback (CPU quantized model) until driver is updated.
  - If node can't join cluster: check bootstrap token TTL and system clock skew: `timedatectl` and NTP reachability.

C) Container runtime and image issues
- Symptoms: images fail to pull, registry auth errors, oom on image unpacking.
- Checks: `docker pull <image>`, `ctr images ls` / `crictl pull`, `journalctl -u docker`
- Fixes:
  - Registry auth: confirm credentials in secret `kubectl get secret reg-creds -n redwood` or static registry config on node.
  - Disk pressure while unpacking: `df -h` and clean `/var/lib/docker` ephemeral caches or increase overlayfs size.

D) Service start / systemd errors
- Symptoms: redwood-agent, redwood-proxy, or onboarding service crashes on start.
- Checks: `systemctl status redwood-agent -l` and `journalctl -u redwood-agent -b`
- Fixes:
  - Missing config: verify `/etc/redwood/config.yaml` is present and has correct TLS cert paths. If certs missing, confirm secret mounts or SSM/KMS retrieval worked during install.
  - Permission denied: check file ownership and SELinux/AppArmor denials (`ausearch` / `auditctl`).

E) Networking: MTU / CNI / Firewall
- Symptoms: periodic timeouts, large message truncation, gRPC stalls.
- Checks: `ip link` MTU, `sysctl net.core.rmem_max`, `iptables -L -n`, traceroute between pods.
- Fixes:
  - MTU mismatch (common in overlay networks): set `network.mtu` in cluster CNI config to 1400 or appropriate value.
  - Firewall blocking ephemeral ports: confirm TCP ranges used by redwood-runtime and kubelet are allowed.

F) Model artifact and KV cache issues
- Symptoms: model loads fail with checksum mismatch or model not found; model server falls back to CPU and OOMs.
- Checks: redwood-model logs, `ls -l /var/lib/redwood/models`, S3/GCS backend connectivity tests.
- Fixes:
  - If checksum mismatch: remove partial artifact and re-download: `rm -rf /var/lib/redwood/models/<model>/parts && redwood-agent fetch-model <model>`
  - If object store auth failed: test `curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' <object-url>` or use the same SDK config as agent.

Upgrade-specific guidance (preflight checklist):
- Backup: snapshot persistent volumes (model caches), backup Terraform remote state (create a tfstate copy), export systemd unit files.
- Drain nodes cleanly: `kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` or equivalent; wait for eviction and KV cache flush.
- Confirm health window: golden traffic test (small set of production requests) and baseline latency metrics.
- Flag bad kernels: maintain a list of supported kernel-driver combos; block upgrade if node has unsupported kernel.

Minimal smoke-tests (post-provision or post-upgrade):
1) Node registration: `kubectl get nodes | grep Ready` expected: all nodes Ready.
2) Agent heartbeat: `curl -sS http://localhost:9080/healthz` on each node expected: `ok`
3) Model load: run a quick generation on a small model pinned to CPU/GPU as appropriate: `redwood-cli generate --model test-tiny --prompt "ping" --max-tokens 8` expected: non-error response within configured latency.
4) Batching path: simulate 5 concurrent short requests to ensure batching doesn't deadlock. Expected: all 5 responses within SLO.
5) Persistent cache checksum: `sha256sum /var/lib/redwood/models/test-tiny/model.bin` — should match value in control plane.

Artifact collection (what to grab before escalation):
- `journalctl -u redwood-agent -b > agent.journal.txt`
- `dmesg > dmesg.txt`
- `kubectl describe node <node> > node.desc.txt` and `kubectl logs -n redwood <pod> --tail=500 > pod.log.txt`
- `/var/log/cloud-init.log` and `/var/log/cloud-init-output.log`
- terraform plan output and `terraform show -json` if available
- compressed model directory `tar czf model.tgz /var/lib/redwood/models/<model>`

Sample small terraform workarounds (copy-paste friendly):
- Force-unlock remote state (only after human check): `terraform force-unlock -force <LOCK_ID>`
- Import an orphaned resource: `terraform import module.node.aws_instance.node i-0abc123` then run `terraform plan`
- Taint and reprovision single resource: `terraform taint module.node.aws_instance.node` then `terraform apply -target=module.node.aws_instance.node`
- Pin provider in root module to avoid auto-upgrade: add to `required_providers` and run `terraform init`

Escalation notes and who to ping:
- If journal shows kernel oops or GPU panic -> page infra-kernel on-call and include `dmesg` and `journalctl -k` extracts.
- If Terraform state corruption -> page infra-terraform owners (linked PR 412) and attach `terraform show -json` and lock ID.
- If model checksum mismatch across nodes -> alert model-ops and attach `sha256` values for both node and control-plane.

Open todos (action items for the runbook):
- Add automated log-collector tool to the agent to output the above artifacts in a single archive.
- Create a small terraform module test harness used during upgrades to exercise import/taint scenarios before touching customer state.
- Expand GPU driver compatibility matrix in Confluence and pin allowed versions in upgrade policy.

Contact and provenance:
- Drafted by: Maya Chen (eng-private-deployments)
- Reviewed: Owen Patel, Lina Rodríguez
- Linked infra PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-modules/pull/412

Notes to self / quick hacks (handy commands):
- Re-run agent registration: `/usr/local/bin/redwood-agent register --config /etc/redwood/config.yaml`
- Check TLS handshake from node to control plane: `openssl s_client -connect controlplane.redwood.local:443 -CAfile /etc/ssl/certs/ca.pem`
- If disk full but you need to keep containers: `docker system prune -af --volumes` (use with caution)

This doc is a working draft — keep it short and practical; move polished procedures into Confluence once validated during actual postmortems.
